messages:
Marina: FYI — planning a small cross-team handoff. We need per-customer observability for Dedicated + Private customers to detect noisy neighbors and drive per-org dashboards. Can infra/runtime teams outline the minimal metric surface we need to start?

Josh: Thanks — main use cases I heard are: 1) noisy neighbor alerts (GPU/CPU steal, queue depth); 2) per-org latency/p99 tail analysis; 3) cost attribution (tokens / GPU-minutes).

Anita: From runtime: we can emit these, but need naming + labels agreed. Propose metrics: `ri_gpu_utilization{org_id=...,device=...,model=...}`, `ri_queue_depth{org_id=...,route=...}`, `ri_rpc_latency_ms_bucket` (histogram), `ri_batch_size_dist`. Thoughts? :eyes:

Kevin: Agree on names. We should include `region` and `model_variant` labels. Also we need `org_id` to be hashed or opaque id — security asked to avoid storing raw customer identifiers in metrics backend.

Oliver: Confirmed — use `org_hash` (sha256 prefix) as the org label. No raw emails/IDs. Also retention note: per-team sensitive dashboards must be access-controlled.

Sasha: From SRE: for noisy neighbor detection we also need per-container GPU memory pressure, kernel preemption counts, and per-queue latency percentiles (50/95/99). If we have eviction_count for KV cache that helps explain regressions.

Rachel: ML/runtime side: add `fallback_count` (counts of model fallbacks) and `kv_cache_hit_ratio{org_hash,model}`. Those are critical to explain perf vs quality tradeoffs.

Josh: Nice. Can someone paste a short mapping for ingestion pipeline? We'll get console/UI folks to prototype tiles.

Anita: Quick ingest sketch (Prometheus -> Metrics Pipeline -> TSDB):
```
metric_name,labelset -> transform -> org_hash label
ri_gpu_utilization{org_hash,device,model,region}
ri_queue_depth{org_hash,route}
ri_rpc_latency_ms_bucket{org_hash,route}
ri_kv_eviction_count{org_hash,model}
ri_fallback_count{org_hash,model}
```
We can emit these immediately from runtime, but need sampling on high-cardinality labels.

Kevin: Implementation note: for high-cardinality orgs we should roll up `org_tier` (free/prod/enterprise) and expose full `org_hash` only for enterprise customers where storage is gated. We'll add `org_tier` as a label for aggregated dashboards.

Marina: UX requirement: console needs a per-org toggle to switch between 'aggregate' and 'per-org' views (permitted only for customers/orgs with access). Also support quick drilldown: click org -> show top N models, top N routes, recent fallbacks.

Josh: For alerting: propose we run a noisy-neighbor detector job that produces `noisy_neighbor_score{org_hash}` once/min, and trigger when score > 0.7 for 5m. Any objections?

Sasha: +1. Define score as weighted sum of queue growth rate, p99 latency delta, GPU steal %. We'll publish the exact formula in a repo README.

Rachel: We'll need labeled example datasets to validate detector — can product/security provide a few red-team/orgs to test?

Marina: Yes, I'll coordinate with CSM to get two opt-in customers and an internal stress test org.

Oliver: Security: ensure metrics ingestion strips any user PII. Also encryption at rest for enterprise metrics.

Anita: Ops question: how do we tag requests to organzations? runtime currently carries `org_id` in request metadata — we'll add logic to emit `org_hash` at the metric emission site to avoid leaking.

Kevin: Timeline/owners proposal:
- Metric spec doc (this week) — Anita + Sasha (owner: Anita)
- Ingest pipeline mapping + rollup policy — Kevin (owner: Kevin) — due EOD next Wed
- Console tiles + drilldown UX mock — Josh + Marina (owner: Josh) — first pass in 2 weeks
- Noisy neighbor detector PoC — Rachel + Sasha (owner: Rachel) — 3 weeks

Josh: Can we also standardize label cardinality limits in the doc (max 3 custom labels per metric, avoid freeform route labels)? That'll help storage.

Anita: Agreed. We'll publish a little linter that fails CI if a new metric uses >3 variable labels.

DeployBot: deploy pipeline status: metrics-collector v2 deployed to staging at 2026-03-19T14:12:00Z :white_check_mark:

Marina: Great — thanks everyone. I'll create a short spec doc and link it here. Action items: Anita (metric emits), Kevin (ingest rollups), Josh (UI proto), Rachel/Sasha (detector PoC). :tada:

Josh: +1, please @ me on the doc.

Sasha: I'll start a small PromQL playground for the detector rules and share queries.

Marina: Last note — please keep dashboards per-org-by-default for enterprise customers, and aggregated for free tier. We'll refine after we see noise in staging.

Kevin: Noted. Cheers.
